why_note_decision: The tweet poses a question, not a factual claim. Netanyahu was alive (he held a press conference on 12 March 2026 and the rumors were debunked by Snopes and Times of Israel) — so the literal answer is 'no', but the tweet isn't asserting otherwise. Replies include people both joking that they wish he were dead and confirming he's alive. The question itself doesn't propagate misinformation; a literal-reading note 'No, he is alive' on a rhetorical question reads as harassment-adjacent moralizing rather than a correction. 28 NNN, 18 OpinionSpeculation, 14 SourcesUnreliable — clear note-not-needed signal.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is a one-line rhetorical question ('So did they kill Netanyahu or not?'), not an assertion that Netanyahu is dead. The viral 'Netanyahu dead' rumor was indeed false (Snopes/Times of Israel — he held a press conference 12 March 2026), but Ana Kasparian is asking, not claiming. Any note that 'corrects' the question by stating Netanyahu is alive treats a question as a factual claim and must FAIL. (Notes that go further and editorialize about her tone are double-fails.)
